A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CogMir research. Their main text, figures, tables, mathematical expressions and appendices are readable and can be matched across formatting changes and subsection renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original LLM experiments on seven cognitive biases, including bias rates in Tables 1–3, information-transmission results and cross-model analyses in Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experimental results and adds two model-response case studies in Appendix D.2.

M1.justification: CogMir retains the same objects, two communication modes, five interaction combinations and bias-rate calculations. Clarifications about simulated participants and evaluators do not establish a changed framework or inference procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same seven cognitive-bias tasks and Known MCQ, Unknown MCQ, Inform, CogScene, CogAction and CogIdentity collections. The new case studies remain within the existing Known/Unknown MCQ Herd Effect coverage.

E2.justification: The seven-model comparison set in Tables 1–2 and the GPT-3.5/GPT-4.0 comparison in Table 3 are unchanged. Newly cited PersonaGym and RoleEval are not evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: New Appendix D.2 cases record an initial answer and then a response to unanimous-A feedback, including correct consensus for the Known MCQ. This adds a limited procedure/control variation alongside the retained Herd templates using B feedback. The main quantitative experiments retain their sample sizes and metrics.

E4.justification: Appendix D.2 adds two qualitative Herd Effect cases contrasting responses to known and uncertain questions. However, the known-question example has peers agreeing with the correct answer, so it does not demonstrate resistance to conflicting group pressure. Existing supplementary model comparisons are retained.

E5.justification: The reported repetition counts, including 50 queries for Known MCQ validation and ten repetitions in the relevant experiments, are retained. v2 adds no new seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 and Figures 3–8 retain their quantitative results. Appendix D.2 adds response-level outcomes: Claude-3 retains answer A on the banana question, while GPT-4 switches from B to A on the future-weather question after unanimous-A feedback.

T1.justification: The channel-capacity expressions and bias-rate definitions, including RateB = M/N and N = p × q, are unchanged. No formal assumptions, propositions, derivations or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion refine the explanatory claim toward 'systematic hallucinations,' explicitly described as structured deviations from factual accuracy. The central CogMir contribution, novelty assertions and claims of prosocial human–agent alignment remain.

C2.justification: New clarifications in Sections 3.2, 4 and 6 explicitly identify simulated human interactions and literature-based human comparisons, qualifying how the alignment claims should be understood. Appendix C.1 explains filtering as a way to exclude pre-existing incorrect beliefs. Existing Appendix B limitations are retained.

D1.justification: v2 documents evaluator expertise, assessment instructions and evaluator temperature zero in Appendix D.1. It also makes the all-50-responses-correct inclusion rule explicit in Appendix C.1 and describes randomly combining synthetic persona attributes in Section 6. These are additional disclosures, without evidence that the existing experiments were rerun.

R1.justification: Section 6.3 adds PersonaGym (Samuel et al., 2024) and RoleEval (Shen et al., 2023) as inspiration for persona construction. The existing related-work discussion and broader research positioning are largely retained.

P1.justification: v2 adds an ethical statement and two introductory Appendix D subsections, expands the Known MCQ explanation, standardizes terminology and changes citation style and author information. Most existing prose and the seven bias-prompt subsections remain substantively intact.

P2.justification: Both versions retain eight figures and seven tables. v2 changes document styling and float placement, revises Figure 2 labels and appendix table captions, and reformats Table 5 with narrower columns and wrapped text. No new result figure or table is introduced.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves transparency by explicitly distinguishing simulated participants from human subjects and better documenting dataset filtering and evaluation. The quantitative evidence is unchanged. The new known-question case provides weak support for resistance to conformity because peers agree with the correct answer, limiting the value of the added analysis. Overall, the documentation gains support a limited improvement.
